The Chemehuevi, who call themselves Nüwüwü, are a Native American people of the eastern Mojave Desert and the lower Colorado River, in California, Nevada and Arizona. They are the southernmost branch of the Southern Paiute and speak a Uto-Aztecan language.

They lived by hunting, gathering desert plants and, near the river, farming, and travelled widely across the desert. In the 1800s many settled in the Colorado River valley beside the Mohave. Their reservation on the river was flooded in 1938 by Lake Havasu, behind the new Parker Dam. Their language is close to that of the Ute.
